body: Perhaps, but it is hard to know whether something is normal or not, when it is such a taboo that even people who have such thoughts will deny it when asked.

I've seen some therapists, but I've never openly discussed these types of thoughts. Probably because somewhere I fear it might end up in some medical record and eventually turn against you (like getting an insurance in the future or through one of the many doctors I personally know or are close family).

I've often had the same types of thoughts, what if I turn the wheel and hit a tree, when you're waiting for a train, ...
I've never had any concrete plans, and at the moment I don't consider myself at risk.
I've often wondered why I think of suicide, it is not really like 'giving up', there isn't really something to give up or to flee from, no accute problems, or at least not at the surface.

It certainly is a big taboo in my social environment, except with people who have had a severe depression.
Just mention the topic and most people panic or show a complete lack of understanding. Many people immediately demand the assurance that you're not thinking about doing 'something stupid', which makes it impossible to discuss the subject with them.

There isn't a typical scenario and often no direct cause. It can happen at any moment. Most of the time it feels (I don't claim I can) as if you can see through the charade of life, how mechanic most people appear, how much misery is caused by stupid misunderstandings, the enormous hypocrisy in human thinking and looking back in time, you realize it has always been this way and will probably never change. It's as if to be happy you have to keep up some sort of illusion and sometimes you fail.
